newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One, Ekkapat deny rumours.
newsitem.headline: Finance One, Ekkapat deny rumours.

text.p: Major Thai finance company, Finance One Plc, denied rumours in the stock market on Friday that it was facing a run on deposits from clients and faced a liquidity crunch.
Another finance firm, Ekkapat Finance and Securities, also denied separately that it was facing liquidity problems.

"We want to deny rumours about any run on our deposits by our major depositors. It is also not true that we offer to borrow funds at the rate of about 20 percent," a senior Finance One official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
Rumours about the health of some finance firms have gripped the Thai stock market since late on Thursday, forcing sales of finance firms and causing the index to drop.
Ekkapat Finance said in a statement to the Thai bourse that it had honoured all its obligations and there were no problems with its cheques. It said the rumours were "groundless."
"The management wants to clarify rumours that the company is experiencing liquidity problems and also that company cheques are not affected," it said.
A major shareholder of Ekkapat is One Holding Plc, the investment arm of Finance One.
Finance One was the most active share traded all day on the stock exchange. It was down 2.50 baht to 23 baht at 0730 GMT.
There were no transactions in Ekkapat shares which closed at 12.75 baht on Thursday.
